workload.shape: 128initial upserts populate64slots per side, then uniform random replacement and20percent delete; fixed disjoint tick bands

method.timed_scope: one normalized array update, top-of-book read and checksum consumption between two clock calls
method.excluded: input generation, text parsing, allocation of workload/timing vectors, book construction and reset, reference checks, serialization, process startup
method.allocation_probe_scope: ordinary replaceable global new/new[] calls during instrumented and aggregate timed loops; not malloc, aligned allocation or OS memory
method.percentile_unit: nanoseconds per instrumented event, pooled across samples
method.instrumentation: empty back-to-back clock-pair distribution measured separately; no subtraction, CPU affinity or isolated host
method.aggregate_scope: separate full-workload loop with one clock pair per batch; median batch time divided by event count is amortized cost, not an event percentile
method.price_scope: bid ticks1000..1063; ask ticks1100..1163; index bands cannot cross, unsupported ticks reject without resizing

limits: A bounded normalized-data implementation experiment, not the legacy replay API or employer code.
Individual clock calls and checksum work affect raw event timings; clock granularity can produce zero observations.
No parser, network, exchange sequencing/recovery, concurrency, order submission or production HFT latency is measured.
No comparison against the legacy map implementation is timed, so no speedup or language ranking is established.
